title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of TSFMs for Electrical Load Forecasting (arXiv 2610.28200), abstract page
note: Abstract page: v1 20 Oct 2026, v2 24 Oct 2026, cs.LG; accepted at IEEE PESS 2026, 6 pages. Headline: pretrained MOIRAI and Chronos-2 beat the implemented seasonal naive and XGBoost baselines at four load aggregation levels; rank-16 LoRA on MOIRAI 1.0 Large lowers NMAE by 7.5% on average with 3.146M trainable weights (about 1%). The page links no code or data.

title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of TSFMs for Electrical Load Forecasting (arXiv 2610.28200), full text v2
note: Design: hourly load from the Worldwide Electricity Load Dataset, Tetouan City and Building Data Genome 2 (2016-2025): 10 national, 13 regional, 25 city or market-zone and 36 building series. Chronological split about 80/10/10 per series; context 2048 h, horizon 96 h, stride 96 h. Temperature over the horizon is a future covariate at city and building level only.

title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of TSFMs for Electrical Load Forecasting (arXiv 2610.28200), full text v2
note: Baselines: weekly seasonal naive (value 168 h earlier) and recursive XGBoost on load lags 1, 24, 168, 336 h plus temperature at city and building level. Metric: NMAE per series (MAE over the series maximum), averaged with equal weight within a level; medians of probabilistic models as point forecasts. No intervals, no significance tests.

title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of TSFMs for Electrical Load Forecasting (arXiv 2610.28200), full text v2
note: Fig. 1, mean NMAE building/city/region/country: seasonal naive 0.1843/0.1854/0.1198/0.1098; XGBoost 0.1432/0.1011/0.0933/0.0696; pretrained MOIRAI Large 0.0752/0.0622/0.0463/0.0383. Small and Base are also below both baselines at every level.

title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of TSFMs for Electrical Load Forecasting (arXiv 2610.28200), full text v2
note: Fig. 2, MOIRAI Large against its pretrained checkpoint: full fine-tuning lowers NMAE by 0.8/10.1/13.8/12.0% (building/city/region/country, to 0.0746/0.0559/0.0399/0.0337); rank-16 LoRA by 0.8/6.3/12.5/10.7% (to 0.0746/0.0583/0.0405/0.0342), 7.5% on average. LoRA ran on a V100 16 GB, full fine-tuning on an A100 80 GB. Ranks 32 to 128, QLoRA and DoRA gave no consistent gain.

title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of TSFMs for Electrical Load Forecasting (arXiv 2610.28200), full text v2
note: Fig. 3, Chronos-2: pretrained NMAE 0.0698/0.0511/0.0388/0.0332 (building/city/region/country), below pretrained MOIRAI Large at every level. Full fine-tuning lowers it by 1.8% on average, LoRA by 4.2% on average, the latter with the best rank per level picked on the test set (rank 128 or 64). 2000 steps, FP16.

title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of TSFMs for Electrical Load Forecasting (arXiv 2610.28200), full text v2
note: Table I, eight held-out series of one year each (Ireland national, a Danish region, a local area, five BDG2 buildings). Pretrained models beat both baselines on all eight by NMAE. Chronos-2 mean NMAE falls from 0.0636 to 0.0504 with LoRA, mostly from the local area and three buildings; the pretrained model stays best on two buildings; national and regional barely change. Best rank per target.

title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of TSFMs for Electrical Load Forecasting (arXiv 2610.28200), full text v2
note: Limitations as the authors state them: one horizon (96 h) and one context; adaptation runs not repeated over seeds; rank comparisons are retrospective test-set ablations; temperature assumed known over the horizon; MOIRAI's pretraining includes BDG2 subsets, so overlap cannot be ruled out. The text names no code repository, adapter weights or results files.

title: Assessing Covariate-Informed Grid Load Forecasting with a Time-Series Foundation Model (arXiv 2609.06656), abstract page (research source)
note: Related study, not a replication: Chronos-2 on ISO New England and ENTSO-E load against task-specific deep models. Abstract: fine-tuning helps Chronos-2 substantially, zero-shot lags the task-specific models, error grows faster with lead. The research call adds that full fine-tuning beat LoRA there, the opposite order to this paper's Chronos-2 result; that detail was not checked in the full text.
